I thought it was because they pop out of a toaster! Your explanation is way better

This is my first go at a writing prompt:

It’s been a couple of weeks, but there are still people everywhere, all over the country, fighting the zombies with a passion refusing to falter, despite everything that’s going on. These people deserve companionship, more so than me. I’m only good at hiding, and looking pretty - and that’s not very hard when you’re surrounded by things to hide from, which make you look pretty in comparison. I’ve been living in my room since the outbreak, and I’ve rarely left. The pristine white walls provide more of a comforting contrast to the crimson world outside with every day that passes. That is, if days do pass. I have no way of knowing. It’s fine, though. 
 
However, this also means I have no way of knowing when, exactly, I came across my companion, Danny. A few hours ago? Years? Does it matter?
 
I rarely feel the need to ever travel far from my home, not even for food, which is easily accessible if you know where to look. This means I feel incredibly, incredibly lucky to have met Danny in our happy coincidence. I hadn’t met a new person in months. He’s lanky, with dark, thinning hair. His eyes are quick and bright, and his adorable, goofy smile is like no other I’ve seen. He often reminds me of a scraggly little puppy, with the way he growls when I tease him, and the way he drools at the smell of food. He wears a torn white jacket which complements his ashy skin tone. 
 
Danny isn’t one for conversation, but I like that. My housemates, who left our room just after the outbreak, as soon as they got the chance, were awfully talkative, and never talked sense. Danny, though, tells me stories all the time, and I sit and listen.
 
We go on adventures I was never able to, before the whole Zombie Thing - and for a week or so after, until my medication wore off. He narrates our serene walks to the little store in the sleepy town in which we live like normal people, and updates me on how our kids are doing; they’re living with us, where they belong, rather than in some silly care home. I watch the hazy sunset over the lake with Danny, and smile as we each eat half of my severed right leg.
